statements.new_statement_en: Appointments to senior state posts should be vetted by an independent committee, even if it can block candidates chosen by elected politicians.

reason: The weighty bills are all about whether senior appointments are controlled by elected politicians or checked by an independent or professional body: civil service appointment method (2, 3, 13), the senior appointments vetting committee (7, 9, 11, 12), the police commissioner search committee (6), and judicial-branch posts (1, 5, 8, 14). The dominant bill (1, about 72% of the weight) changes how the judges' ombudsman is chosen, and bill 5 gives the choice of Supreme Court president to the Knesset. In both, power moves to the Knesset or to politicians in general, not to ministers. Changing 'elected ministers' to 'elected politicians' covers these bills with the smallest possible change and keeps the agree key. Bill 4 (diversity on government company boards) is off-topic but light.
